## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

We should build a static HTML game. Fully offline smash bros clone with local 2-player and CPUs. Vanilla JS with canvas 2D, no external assets. Need to create index.html, styles, game.js. Should be high quality: platforms, characters, moves (jab, tilt, smash, special), shields, dodges, knockback %, stocks, blast zones, particles, sound via WebAudio (offline, synthesized), menus, character select, stage select, pause, results. AI opponents. Local multiplayer on keyboard, gamepad support perhaps.

Design:

- Canvas 2D rendering with procedural characters (no images), cool visual style: gradient sky, parallax mountains, stage with platforms.
- 4 players max, humans + CPUs.
- Characters: 4-6 with distinct stats and specials.
- Physics: gravity, friction, air control, jumps (double jump), fast fall, dash, shields, dodges, hitstun, knockback formula akin Smash.

- Input mapping: P1 WASD + F/G/H, P2 arrows + numpad/period. Gamepad support using navigator.getGamepads.
- Audio synth: hits, jumps, KO, menu music maybe simple loops? Keep subtle. Mute toggle.
- Menus: title -> character select (4 slots choose human/CPU) -> stage select -> battle. Use DOM overlay UI? Could do canvas UI entirely. DOM easier for menus and accessibility. But game feel better all-canvas. I'll do DOM overlay for menus with styled cards, plus in-game HUD drawn on canvas? HUD can be DOM too. Canvas for the game, HUD DOM for each player (damage, stocks, portrait). Pause overlay DOM.

We need a single "Start" button visible on load that starts gameplay directly (auto-start capture clicks "Start" or "Play"). Since it clicks the only eligible button, if there are multiple visible buttons only Start/Play matching count. On title screen, have "Start" button that goes to character select? Capture would then screenshot char select, not gameplay. Better: title screen with "Start" that begins a quick match immediately? But we want menus. Hmm, capture auto starts by clicking "Start" once and screenshot after 1s. For our own check we can script clicks with playwright manually. The final capture for the system might click start then game starts. We can make title screen "Play" button go directly into a default match (P1 vs CPU) to ensure gameplay screenshot. And a "Custom Match" button opens character select. That yields good capture: click Play -> battle starts immediately. Also character select reachable. Alternatively title "Start" opens mode select but not gameplay. I'd rather have Play = quick match.

We should ensure keyboard/menu UI. Also note capture clicks only exactly Start/Play labeled buttons. We'll have primary button "Play" plus others ("Custom Match", "How to Play"). Autostart clicks Play -> immediate game. Good.

Gameplay details plan:

Characters (4):
1. Blaze (balanced fire martial artist): jab, fireball neutral special, rising uppercut up special.
2. Volt (fast electric ninja): quick, low weight, dash attack, thunder special.
3. Glacier (heavy penguin/brute): slow, heavy, hammer smash, ice breath.
4. Sprout (floaty plant): mid, projectile seed, floaty jumps.
Maybe 5th: Nova (sword) - keep 4 to polish.

Stages (3):
- Sky Sanctum: main platform + 2 floating platforms.
- Ember Foundry: main + side platforms.
- Frozen Peaks: slopes? Keep flat main platform but varied platform layout. Add hazards? no.

Rendering: canvas 2D at DPR scaling. Camera follows players, zoom dynamic. World units ~ 1280x720 logical. Stage width ~ 1600. Camera clamp, zoom 0.75-1.1.

Character rendering: procedural vector art, distinct head/body/colors, limbs animated based on state (run cycle, jumps, attack poses). Draw shadow, afterimages for dash, particles.

Combat:
- Each move definition: startup frames, active frames, recovery, damage, base knockback, growth, angle, hitbox offset, size, hitstop, shieldstun.
- Attack stages: jab combo (3 hits), side tilt, up tilt, down tilt? Keep jab, side, up, down aerial, neutral special, side special maybe. Simplify inputs:
  - Attack key (J / button) + direction = directional attacks. Neutral attack = jab; forward = dash slash; up = up tilt; down = crouch kick; in air = neutral air; up air; down air (spike).
  - Special key: neutral special (projectile), up special (recovery), side special (dash), down special (counter/ground pound?). Implement neutral + up specials per character; side special shared archetype dash attack with character effect; down special maybe parry/counter for all? Keep "neutral special" and "up special" distinct, side/down generic.
  - Shield key (K/shift): hold shield, reduces damage/knockback, drains shield meter, breaks if depleted. Dodges with direction while shielding? Roll on L/R. Simpler: shield key + direction triggers dodge with i-frames; double-tap? Use dodge key (L).
  - Grab? skip maybe. Smash attacks? Charge smash by holding attack while direction? Add charged smash: hold attack key while pressing direction -> charge up to 60 frames, release. Implement hold-to-charge for forward/down/up attacks on ground. Show charge glow. This adds depth.

Knockback formula: kb = ((percent/100 * 0.5 + 0.5) * (base + growth * percent/100)) roughly. Use hitstun = kb*0.35 frames. Launch velocity = kb * factor.
Blast zones: |x|>1050, y<-600, y>700 relative to stage. Stage center world 0,0; main platform y=0 top surface. Draw ground.

Stocks 3 default (custom 1-5). Damage percent UI.

Match flow: 3..2..1..GO countdown, battle, KO -> respawn at top with 2s invincible, match end when one remains/stock all gone -> results screen with rematch/menu.

AI: state machine with difficulty. Behaviors: approach target, spacing, attack when in range, shield occasionally, jump recovery, recover using up special, avoid edge, pick projectiles at distance. Simple but decent. Need AI to not be braindead: choose nearest opponent, move toward, attack, sometimes jump, use specials, recover when offstage.

Input system: actions Left/Right/Up/Down, Jump, Attack, Special, Shield, Dodge, Pause. Keyboard mapping:
P1: WASD, F jump? Common: WASD move, Space jump? But space scrolls; prevent default. Use W jump, A/D move, S crouch/fastfall. Attack J, Special K, Shield L, Dodge Shift. Hmm shield L and dodge shift.
P2: Arrow keys, numpad? Many keyboards. Use Arrows + [1] attack? Better: Arrows, Comma jump? Let's define P2: Arrow keys, "/" jump, "." attack? Awkward. Use numpad: 4/6 movement? Arrow keys + numpad 1 attack, 2 special, 3 shield, 0 dodge, numpad 0 jump? Hmm.

Simpler P2: Arrows move, ArrowUp jump, `[` attack? Use numpad: Numpad0 jump, Numpad1 attack, Numpad2 special, Numpad3 shield, Numpad5 dodge. Since arrows + numpad are right side. Document on UI. Also gamepad support for players.

Also allow P1 gamepad index 0 etc. Buttons: A jump, X/Y attack, B special, RB shield, LB dodge, start pause.

Gamepad polling.

Sound: WebAudio synth, starting after first user gesture. Sounds: menu click, countdown beep, hit (noise burst + osc), KO (falling boom), jump, shield, projectile, KO crowd. Also a simple procedural background loop? Offline. Could compose a chiptune loop with oscillators scheduled. Nice but complexity; implement a small music sequencer with a catchy battle theme, toggleable. Keep volume low. Match vibe.

Visual polish:
- Background layers with parallax: sky gradient, sun, clouds, distant floating islands, foreground particles.
- Stage platform with depth, glowing edges, underside.
- Hit effects: impact stars, slash arcs, dust, damage numbers floating, screen shake, hitstop, slow-mo KO zoom maybe gradient flash.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files

## Objective
- Build a complete, fully offline, Super Smash Bros.–style platform fighter with local multiplayer, CPUs, stages, menus, and synthesized audio.

- Fully playable and offline.
- No asking for clarifications.
- Include visual polish and reasonable local game assumptions.

- Use HTML canvas with procedural artwork and Web Audio synthesis.
- Support keyboard and gamepad inputs.
